intro: Week 6 ended with the AFC North in a three-way tie at 4-2 after Cleveland beat Baltimore on the final kick. Kansas City is 5-0 and Minnesota took its bye unbeaten, while the Chargers fell to 0-6 and the Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the season. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Browns beat the Ravens 13-10 on a walk-off field goal
top.dek: Cleveland trailed 10-0 at halftime and scored 13 unanswered points. Deshaun Watson hit Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards to set up Andre Szmyt's 37-yard kick as time expired. The Browns, Ravens and Steelers now sit tied at 4-2 atop the AFC North.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Giants lose quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season
top.dek: Dart is out for the year with a knee injury. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor also missed Sunday's loss to the Saints with a calf injury, and Marcus Mbow started in his place.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Chad Ryland kicks six field goals, the last one at the buzzer
top.dek: The Cardinals kicker made all six attempts at SoFi, finishing with a 43-yarder as time ran out to beat the Rams. His six kicks accounted for all 18 of Arizona's points.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 100: Mahomes ties Brady for the youngest quarterback to 100 wins
top.dek: Patrick Mahomes earned career win No. 100 in the 22-6 victory over the Chargers. He finished 23 of 30 for 272 yards with one interception as Kansas City moved to 5-0.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs visit the Seahawks on Sunday Night Football
top.dek: Kansas City and Seattle meet Sunday, Oct. 25, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC from Lumen Field. The Chiefs are 5-0 and Seattle is 3-3 after an overtime loss to Denver.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Allen ties Kelly as Bills go into bye 5-1

stories.text: Allen ties Jim Kelly's franchise TD pass record in Vegas
stories.summary: Josh Allen threw two touchdown passes in a 33-30 win at Las Vegas, which put him level with Jim Kelly at 258 for the Bills. Buffalo moved to 5-1 and finished its West Coast trip with two road wins. Allen's five-game streak of rushing touchdowns ended one short of the Super Bowl-era record.

stories.text: Moore and Oliver miss a second straight game
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) and defensive lineman Ed Oliver (knee) did not play for the second week in a row. Bradley Chubb (ribs) and Dalton Kincaid (ribs) each left briefly and came back. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was removed late in the first half for unsportsmanlike conduct, and coach Joe Brady said the team will address it.

stories.text: James Cook scores the go-ahead touchdown
stories.summary: Cook ran 22 times for 95 yards and scored from 3 yards out in the fourth quarter. He also caught all three of his targets for 58 yards, his best receiving day of 2026. Keon Coleman added a touchdown on Allen's shovel pass in the third quarter.

stories.text: 0: turnovers for Buffalo against the Raiders
stories.summary: The Bills played their first turnover-free game of the season after giving the ball away nine times in the previous three weeks. The clean day helped Buffalo hold off a Raiders rally led by Kirk Cousins, who threw for 313 yards.

stories.text: Bye week, then Ravens at Highmark
stories.summary: Buffalo is off this week. The Bills host Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET. Watch whether Moore and Oliver are back after the extra rest.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins use the bye to heal and reset

stories.text: Winless Dolphins say execution, not effort, is the problem
stories.summary: Miami is 0-5 and has trailed by seven or fewer entering the fourth quarter in each of its last three games. Malik Willis said youth is no longer an excuse and the team can't keep leaning on late comebacks. The bye gives the staff a week to clean up mistakes.

stories.text: Eight injured Dolphins get a week to recover
stories.summary: The bye gives eight injured players time to heal. Receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle), running back Jaylen Wright (foot) and cornerback Storm Duck are aiming to return against the Jets. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks hurt his foot against Cincinnati but came back into that game.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon II gives Miami a ground game
stories.summary: Gordon ran 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the 31-24 loss to Cincinnati. Miami's rushing attack has averaged 5.5 yards per carry since Week 3, third best in the league.

stories.text: 4: sacks for the Dolphins defense through five games
stories.summary: That is Miami's lowest total through five games since at least 1981. The defense has also allowed a 76.0 percent completion rate, which is on pace to threaten the NFL record.

stories.text: Dolphins visit the Jets in Week 7
stories.summary: Miami is on bye this week. The Dolphins play at the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at MetLife Stadium. Four of their next six games are against AFC East teams.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots beat Jets for a third straight win

stories.text: Patriots hold off Jets 26-19 for third straight win
stories.summary: New England led 17-3 at halftime and survived a late Jets push to reach 4-2. The Patriots have beaten New York four straight times and 19 of the last 21. A.J. Brown returned from injured reserve and Christian Gonzalez was back after missing two games.

stories.text: Doubs, Moses and Vera-Tucker leave early
stories.summary: Receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) left in the first quarter after his touchdown and did not return. Tackle Morgan Moses (ankle) and guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) also went out in the second quarter, and Vera-Tucker was ruled out. Ben Brown (knee) was helped off in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws three TDs again
stories.summary: Maye went 18 of 32 for 235 yards and three touchdowns, his third straight game with at least three scoring passes. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry each caught one. Douglas led the team with seven catches for 86 yards.

stories.text: 19: Patriots wins in the last 21 meetings with the Jets
stories.summary: New England has won the last four in the series. A.J. Brown had a quiet return, with three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets and three drops.

stories.text: Short week: Patriots at Bears on Thursday night
stories.summary: New England visits Chicago on Thursday, Oct. 22, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch the offensive line, which lost Moses and Vera-Tucker during the Jets game.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets fall short in Foxborough, 26-19

stories.text: Jets fall to 2-4 after slow start in New England
stories.summary: The Jets trailed 17-3 at halftime and 23-13 in the fourth quarter before cutting it to 23-19. They went 0 for 3 in the red zone and failed on two early fourth-down tries. Coach Aaron Glenn pointed to finishing and defensive detail.

stories.text: Mauigoa leaves with thigh injury, Hall sits again
stories.summary: Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa left in the first quarter with a thigh injury. Running back Breece Hall (quad) and receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) were inactive. Omar Cooper Jr. returned from an ankle injury that had kept him on injured reserve.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. posts first 100-yard game
stories.summary: In his first game back from injured reserve, Cooper caught six passes for 103 yards, including a 48-yard touchdown from Geno Smith. Smith finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards.

stories.text: 166: passes before Geno Smith threw an interception
stories.summary: Smith's first pick of the season went to Charles Woods and sealed the Patriots win. Until then he had gone the longest stretch of his career without one.

stories.text: Jets host the Dolphins at MetLife
stories.summary: New York hosts winless Miami on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch for Hall's status and whether the offense finishes drives in the red zone.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens waste a 10-0 lead in Cleveland

stories.text: Ravens lose 13-10 in Cleveland on a walk-off field goal
stories.summary: Baltimore scored on its first two drives, led 10-0 at halftime and never scored again. Derrick Henry fumbled in the fourth quarter, Tyler Loop missed a long field goal, and Andre Szmyt hit a 37-yarder as time expired. The Ravens fell to 4-2 and now share first place in the AFC North with Cleveland.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson sits again with a day-to-day ankle injury
stories.summary: Jackson has not practiced since hurting his ankle 12 days before the Browns game and missed his second straight start. Coach Jesse Minter called him day-by-day, and Baltimore hopes to have him back next week. Rashod Bateman left Sunday's game with an injury after barely playing, and the Ravens also played without tight end Matt Hibner, center Cam Jurgens and tackle Broderick Washington.

stories.text: Tyler Huntley keeps the offense moving, but not far enough
stories.summary: Starting for Jackson, Huntley went 19-of-31 for 165 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland. Josh Cuevas caught the score. Baltimore managed just 10 points, all of them before halftime.

stories.text: 15: fourth-quarter leads of seven or more the Ravens have blown since 2020
stories.summary: That is the most in the NFL over that span, according to CBS Sports. Sunday added another one. Baltimore held Cleveland to 46 first-half yards and still lost.

stories.text: Bengals visit Baltimore on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati arrives off its Week 6 bye at 3-2. The Ravens run the ball well, averaging 164.4 rushing yards per game, third in the league. Watch whether Jackson's ankle allows him to return.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals rest up before a trip to Baltimore

stories.text: Bengals use the bye to fix their run defense
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 3-2 and idle in Week 6 after a run of close games. Coach Zac Taylor said the break came at a good time and that the run defense needs work after Miami gained over 200 rushing yards in a 31-24 Bengals win. Baltimore is next, and the Ravens lost in Cleveland on Sunday.

stories.text: Tight end Tanner Hudson likely done for the season
stories.summary: Hudson tore a pectoral muscle in the Week 5 win over Miami, and his agent told ESPN he will likely miss the rest of the year. He was the fourth tight end on the depth chart behind Drew Sample, Mike Gesicki and Erick All Jr. Hudson played 20 to 25 snaps a game and worked on special teams.

stories.text: Joe Burrow sits sixth in the NFL in passing yards
stories.summary: Through five games Burrow has 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions. He threw four touchdown passes in the Week 5 win at Miami. Hudson, Gesicki, Samaje Perine and Ja'Marr Chase all caught scores.

stories.text: 82.8: Bengals rushing yards per game, 26th in the NFL
stories.summary: Cincinnati throws for 260.0 yards a game, but the ground attack has lagged. Baltimore runs for 164.4 per game, third in the league. That gap shapes Sunday's matchup.

stories.text: Bengals at Ravens, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at M&T Bank Stadium after Cincinnati's bye. A win would put the Bengals at 4-2. Watch the Baltimore quarterback situation and whether the Bengals can slow Derrick Henry.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns take a share of first in the AFC North

stories.text: Szmyt's field goal as time expires beats the Ravens 13-10
stories.summary: Cleveland trailed 10-0 at halftime and scored 13 unanswered points. Audric Estime tied it with a 2-yard run, and Deshaun Watson hit Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards to set up Andre Szmyt's 37-yard kick. The Browns are 4-2 and tied with Baltimore and Pittsburgh atop the division.

stories.text: Delpit in concussion protocol, Jefferson hurt his hip
stories.summary: Safety Grant Delpit left in the first quarter and entered the concussion protocol. Linebacker Justin Jefferson hurt his hip. Carson Schwesinger played through an ankle sprain after being listed questionable.

stories.text: Carson Schwesinger turns the game with a forced fumble
stories.summary: Schwesinger finished with 13 tackles and stripped Derrick Henry in the fourth quarter. Tyson Campbell recovered, and Estime scored the tying touchdown on the next drive. Schwesinger did it on a sprained ankle.

stories.text: 46: yards the Browns gained in the first half Sunday
stories.summary: Cleveland also had just three first downs before the break and trailed 10-0. The offense found its footing late, with Watson throwing for 94 of his 164 yards in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Browns at Titans, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at Nissan Stadium in Nashville. Cleveland is 2-0 in the AFC North. Watch the health of the defense, with Delpit in protocol.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers rally from 13 down to win in overtime

stories.text: Steelers storm back to beat Tampa Bay 26-19 in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 entering the fourth quarter. Boswell kicked field goals of 58 and 20 yards to take the lead, Tampa tied it, and Aaron Rodgers hit Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown in overtime. The Steelers are 4-2 and share first place.

stories.text: Jalen Ramsey plays on a broken wrist, McCarthy rolls an ankle
stories.summary: Ramsey had two sacks while playing with a broken wrist. Coach Mike McCarthy appeared to sprain his ankle at the end of the first half. Wide receiver Roman Wilson is on injured reserve, which left the group thin.

stories.text: DK Metcalf catches 11 passes for 93 yards
stories.summary: Metcalf was a late addition to the injury report with an illness and played anyway. He converted a 20-yard catch on third-and-13 in overtime. Rodgers leaned on him while the offense sputtered for three quarters.

stories.text: 13: points Pittsburgh trailed by entering the fourth quarter
stories.summary: The Steelers were down 16-3 and still won. CBS Sports called it their largest fourth-quarter comeback since 2002. Their defense held Tampa Bay to 116 first-half yards.

stories.text: Steelers face the Saints in Paris, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: The game is at the Stade de France and airs on NFL Network, with New Orleans as the designated home team. The Saints are 2-4 after beating the Giants. Watch how Jaylen Warren and the run game fare against New Orleans.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Fairbairn's kick beats Jacksonville at Wembley

stories.text: Fairbairn wins it at the horn in London
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired and Houston beat Jacksonville 34-31 at Wembley Stadium. The Texans have won two straight after an 0-4 start. C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to Foster Moreau.

stories.text: Blankenship ruled out with a concussion
stories.summary: Safety Reed Blankenship left in the second quarter for a concussion check, was first listed questionable, then was ruled out about 30 minutes later. M.J. Stewart took his snaps. Linebacker and captain Azeez Al-Shaair also went through a concussion evaluation but came back in the second half.

stories.text: Stroud plays his best game in years
stories.summary: Stroud went 24 of 34 for 312 yards and three touchdowns, with his first interception of the season coming in the end zone late. Jaylin Noel caught four passes for 107 yards and a score, and Marvin Harrison Jr. had three catches for 34 yards in his debut after the trade from Arizona.

stories.text: 35.6%: Houston's heavy line usage leads the NFL
stories.summary: The Texans lined up six or more offensive linemen on 35.6 percent of their plays, the highest rate of any team this season. The approach paid off on the ground. Houston ran for 114 yards, and Woody Marks became the first back to top 40 rushing yards against Jacksonville this year.

stories.text: Giants visit NRG Stadium Sunday at 1 ET on FOX
stories.summary: Houston hosts the New York Giants on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Texans then have their Week 8 bye. Watch whether Harrison Jr. and Nico Collins keep sharing targets with Noel.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts blow a 13-0 lead and get booed at home

stories.text: Colts lose to winless Titans 26-20
stories.summary: Indianapolis led 13-0 at halftime and lost to a Tennessee team that had no wins. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown gave the Titans their first lead. Shane Steichen called the loss extremely disappointing and said the fixes have to come fast. Fans booed, and the coach said he understood why.

stories.text: Sauce Gardner leaves with a calf injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner went down with a calf injury in the third quarter and did not return, with Cam Taylor-Britt taking over. Punter Rigoberto Sanchez hurt his foot on the blocked punt, and returner Anthony Gould entered concussion protocol. Tight end Tyler Warren sat out with a groin injury.

stories.text: Daniel Jones struggles against the Titans rush
stories.summary: Jones went 22 of 42 for 269 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, and he took six sacks. The NFL.com recap lists him at four touchdown passes and six interceptions on the season. Two Hail Mary tries at the end fell incomplete.

stories.text: 6: sacks Indianapolis allowed to Tennessee
stories.summary: Jones was sacked six times and hit 11 times in the loss. The Colts' line also drew a holding penalty that put them in second-and-20 during a stalled drive. Protection is the most fixable problem on this offense.

stories.text: Colts open a road trip at Minnesota
stories.summary: Indianapolis visits the Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1:00 p.m. ET to start a two-game road trip. Week 8 brings a divisional game at Jacksonville on Nov. 1. The Colts are 0-2 in the AFC South.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lose a shootout at Wembley

stories.text: Jaguars drop a 34-31 game on the final kick
stories.summary: Jacksonville lost to Houston when Ka'imi Fairbairn made a 49-yard field goal as time ran out. Cam Little had tied the game from 60 yards with 1:55 left. The loss ended a three-game winning streak and cost the Jaguars their AFC South lead.

stories.text: Anton Harrison goes on IR with a knee injury
stories.summary: Left tackle Anton Harrison landed on injured reserve after a noncontact right knee injury in the win over Philadelphia. He faces at least four missed games and is expected to need arthroscopic surgery once the team returns from London. Long snapper Ross Matiscik also sat out with a shoulder injury, and Jacob Bobenmoyer filled in.

stories.text: Travis Hunter scores and intercepts in one game
stories.summary: Hunter caught a 7-yard touchdown from Trevor Lawrence and later picked off C.J. Stroud in the end zone. Few players have done both in a single game. Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns, two of them to Bhayshul Tuten.

stories.text: 426: yards allowed by the No. 2 scoring defense
stories.summary: Jacksonville came in with the NFL's second-best scoring defense and gave up 426 yards to Houston. The Texans scored touchdowns on three of their four drives from the second quarter through the fourth. Houston also rushed for 114 yards, the most the Jaguars have allowed on the ground this season.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Colts on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Jacksonville is off in Week 7, which Lawrence said gives the team time to reflect. The Jaguars host Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET. Network was not listed in the schedule source.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans finally win, Saleh gets his first

stories.text: Titans beat Colts 26-20 for Saleh's first win
stories.summary: Tennessee trailed 13-0 at halftime and came back in Indianapolis. Chimere Dike's 58-yard punt return set up the tying score, and Oluwafemi Oladejo returned a blocked punt for the touchdown that gave the Titans their first lead. Joey Slye's field goals from 49 and 44 yards late sealed it. The win ended a six-game losing streak to the Colts.

stories.text: Hooker returns, Winston stays out with a quad
stories.summary: Safety Amani Hooker came back from a concussion and finished with a career-high 13 tackles and an interception. Safety Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) was ruled out on Friday's report, and Tyjae Spears (knee) was questionable. Safety Tony Adams and cornerback Marcus Harris left in the first half and returned.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons wrecks the Colts' game plan
stories.summary: Simmons had six tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. His hit on Jonathan Taylor produced a second-half turnover. Jermaine Johnson II added two sacks as Tennessee finished with six as a team.

stories.text: 102: the fewest passing yards by a winning QB this year
stories.summary: Cam Ward went 11 of 22 for 102 yards, the lowest total from a winning quarterback this season according to Sumer Sports. He still threw a touchdown to Carnell Tate and led a seven-play, 52-yard drive for the go-ahead points. The Titans managed only 186 total yards.

stories.text: Browns visit Nissan Stadium Sunday at 1 ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Cleveland on Sunday, Oct. 25 at noon CT (1:00 p.m. ET) on CBS. Robert Saleh said he wants the team to build on what worked and fix what did not. Watch whether the offense can produce more than 186 yards.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win Thursday night in overtime

stories.text: Broncos survive Seattle in overtime, 17-14
stories.summary: Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Sam Darnold in overtime and Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal to beat the Seahawks on Thursday night. Denver led 14-3 at halftime, then watched Seattle score 11 straight and tie it on a Jason Myers kick with 3 seconds left. The win moves the Broncos to 4-2.

stories.text: Surtain and Hufanga both sit out with ankle injuries
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II has played through an ankle problem since Week 4 and was ruled out Thursday after not practicing. Safety Talanoa Hufanga hurt his ankle in the Week 5 win over the Chargers, and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported he could miss about three weeks. Surtain could return against Arizona, but Denver has not confirmed that.

stories.text: McMillian ends it with an overtime interception
stories.summary: Ja'Quan McMillian grabbed Sam Darnold's pass in overtime to hand Lutz the game-winning try. Denver's defense sacked Darnold five times and hit him 17 times, and Kris Abrams-Draine also intercepted him late in regulation.

stories.text: 168: total yards for a Broncos offense that still won
stories.summary: Denver gained 168 yards, less than half of Seattle's 353. Bo Nix went 17 of 27 for 107 yards, and J.K. Dobbins ran for 41 yards and a touchdown. The defense and the kicker did the rest.

stories.text: Broncos head to Arizona on Sunday
stories.summary: Denver visits the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS (regional broadcast) at State Farm Stadium. Watch the status of Surtain and Hufanga in the secondary.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs stay unbeaten, beat Chargers 22-6

stories.text: Chiefs beat Chargers 22-6 to move to 5-0
stories.summary: Kansas City led 19-3 at halftime at Arrowhead and cruised past winless Los Angeles. The Chiefs sit atop the AFC West with a 1.5 game lead over Denver. The offense was steady rather than sharp, and Patrick Mahomes threw an end-zone interception.

stories.text: Rice and Thornton out, Kelce's ankle bears watching
stories.summary: Receivers Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) were out Sunday, and Rice's availability is uncertain going forward. Travis Kelce had his ankle worked on several times and was slow to get up after one play, though no diagnosis was reported. Left tackle Josh Simmons was also out, per Arrowhead Addict.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker keeps running the Chiefs offense
stories.summary: Walker carried 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns, including a 33-yarder in the first quarter. He now has 665 rushing yards on the season, and he led the league in yards per carry entering the week.

stories.text: 100: Mahomes ties Brady for fastest to 100 wins
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes earned his 100th career win, tying Tom Brady as the youngest quarterback to reach it. He finished 23 of 30 for 272 yards with one interception.

stories.text: Chiefs travel to Seattle for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Kansas City plays the defending champion Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC from Lumen Field. Rice's hamstring is the question to track this week.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders lose third straight, 33-30 to Bills

stories.text: Raiders drop third straight, 33-30 to Bills
stories.summary: Las Vegas fell to 3-3 after starting 3-0 and has lost three in a row. Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns, but James Cook's 3-yard run put Buffalo ahead for good. The Raiders now sit ahead of only the winless Chargers in the division.

stories.text: Jeanty's foot was the pregame concern
stories.summary: Ashton Jeanty entered the game with a foot issue after aggravating his ankle in Week 4, and he practiced fully before Sunday. Coach Klint Kubiak said flatly that Jeanty was playing. No Raiders injuries were reported in the postgame game story.

stories.text: Michael Mayer posts a career-high 95 yards
stories.summary: The tight end caught seven passes for 95 yards, a career best. Tre Tucker added five catches for 97 yards and a 44-yard touchdown, and Brock Bowers finished with 70 yards on four catches.

stories.text: 313: Cousins yards in a losing effort
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins completed 23 of 41 passes for 313 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He led a 91-yard touchdown drive late to tie the game at 23. Rookie Fernando Mendoza is not expected to take over soon.

stories.text: Rams visit Allegiant Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET (1:25 p.m. PT) on FOX. The Raiders need to stop the slide and fix a defense that keeps giving back leads.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers fall to 0-6 in Kansas City

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-6 with 22-6 loss at Kansas City
stories.summary: Los Angeles trailed 19-3 at half and never found the end zone. A 57-yard Quentin Johnston catch set up goal-to-go, but the drive ended in a field goal, and a later series died on downs inside the 10. The Chargers get a Week 7 bye to regroup.

stories.text: Receiver room is thin before the bye
stories.summary: Before the Chiefs game, Brenen Thompson and KeAndre Lambert-Smith were listed questionable, and Tre' Harris left the Week 5 loss with a hamstring injury. Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were cleared to play. Statuses after Sunday were not available in the sources.

stories.text: Quentin Johnston's 57-yarder is the lone big play
stories.summary: Johnston's 57-yard catch was the Chargers' longest play of the season. The offense could not turn it into a touchdown, which sums up the year so far.

stories.text: 8: Herbert interceptions through six games
stories.summary: Justin Herbert threw for 204 yards with no touchdowns and an interception Sunday, his eighth of the season. Kansas City opened with three Harrison Butker field goals and two Kenneth Walker touchdown runs.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Rams
stories.summary: The Chargers are off in Week 7. They return Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Rams at SoFi Stadium.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys drop second straight at Lambeau

stories.text: Cowboys fall to 2-4 after Sunday night loss in Green Bay
stories.summary: Dallas lost 23-13 to the Packers and has dropped two in a row for the first time this season, after Thursday night's loss to Tampa Bay. Green Bay led 17-0 at the half, and the Cowboys converted just 4 of 11 third downs. Dak Prescott threw two interceptions and the Packers pressured him on 21 dropbacks.

stories.text: Prescott says ribs took a hit but he stayed in
stories.summary: Prescott said he banged up his left ribs on the Cowboys' last drive in Green Bay and got the wind knocked out of him. He took no medical attention and finished the game. Watch his practice participation this week ahead of Monday's trip to Philadelphia.

stories.text: Prescott throws 54 times and still can't find a rhythm
stories.summary: Prescott finished 34 of 54 for 258 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Both picks led to first-half Packers points, a field goal and a one-yard Jordan Love touchdown run. He was hit seven times, and a late throw sailed out of the end zone on a turnover on downs.

stories.text: 18: targets for CeeDee Lamb, who turned them into 70 yards
stories.summary: Lamb caught 9 of 18 targets for 70 yards and no touchdowns against Green Bay. George Pickens added 6 catches for 73 yards on 11 targets, and Ryan Flournoy scored on 7 catches for 40. Dallas managed only 13 points, its lowest total of the season.

stories.text: Cowboys visit the Eagles on Monday night
stories.summary: Dallas plays at Philadelphia on Monday, Oct. 26, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC at Lincoln Financial Field. Both teams are 2-4. Watch whether the Cowboys can protect Prescott against an Eagles team starting Tanner McKee.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Winston benched as McCarthy nearly rallies Giants

stories.text: Giants bench Winston, McCarthy rally falls short vs. Saints
stories.summary: New Orleans beat the Giants 34-27. Jameis Winston went 14 of 26 with two interceptions before John Harbaugh pulled him, and J.J. McCarthy led 17 unanswered points. Harbaugh would not name a starter for the next game.

stories.text: Dart is out for the season, Eluemunor sits with a calf
stories.summary: Quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the year with a knee injury. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor missed Sunday with a calf injury, and Marcus Mbow started in his place. A defensive starter also left the game, though the report did not name him.

stories.text: McCarthy: 243 yards in about 11 minutes of work
stories.summary: McCarthy, acquired last month from Minnesota for a fifth-round pick, went 11 of 21 for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He also led the Giants with 26 rushing yards. His fourth-and-1 throw to Isaiah Likely in the end zone fell incomplete with 12 seconds left.

stories.text: 5: fumbles lost by the Giants this season, on 11 total
stories.summary: Sunday's kickoff fumble was the Giants' 11th of the year and their fifth lost. The ground game added little too, with running backs getting 14 carries for 34 yards. Harbaugh's group trailed 34-10 before the late push.

stories.text: Giants head to Houston with a quarterback question
stories.summary: New York plays at the Texans on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Harbaugh has not picked between Winston and McCarthy. The Giants still lead the NFC East at 3-2-1.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles lose fourth straight, Hurts on IR

stories.text: Eagles lose 25-14 to Panthers for a fourth straight loss
stories.summary: Philadelphia fell to 2-4 and has its first four-game losing streak since 2020. Tanner McKee made his first meaningful start in place of Jalen Hurts and went 26 of 45 for 215 yards with one touchdown and three sacks.

stories.text: Hurts on IR with a calf clot, three more hurt Sunday
stories.summary: Hurts is on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot in his calf and has no return timeline. The team's own site says he will miss at least the next three games. Carson Steele (shoulder), Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion) and Jordan Davis (right leg) were all ruled out during the game.

stories.text: DeVonta Smith hauls in a touchdown on seven catches
stories.summary: Smith caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown from McKee in the loss. Several McKee throws were wiped out by penalties, including a 20-yard pass to Darius Cooper called back for holding. Dameon Pierce scored his first touchdown since 2024.

stories.text: 35: rushing yards for the Eagles against Carolina
stories.summary: Philadelphia ran for only 35 yards with Hurts out, which left McKee carrying the offense through the air. The Eagles dropped to 2-4 and have lost four straight for the first time in six seasons.

stories.text: Eagles host Cowboys on Monday night, then Washington
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts Dallas on Monday, Oct. 26, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. The Eagles' next three games are all against NFC East opponents. McKee remains the starter.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders at unbeaten 49ers on Monday night

stories.text: Commanders face unbeaten 49ers after a costly tie
stories.summary: Washington visits San Francisco tonight at 1-3-1, a week after a 27-27 overtime tie with the Giants. Dan Quinn took responsibility for the final play, a pass call in which Jayden Daniels was sacked with no timeouts left to spike the ball.

stories.text: Four Commanders out, nine questionable for 49ers
stories.summary: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) are out. Stefon Diggs is questionable after limited work Friday and Saturday. Washington is also waiting on Trey Amos and Jordan Magee to be activated from the reserve list.

stories.text: Daniels runs for 103 yards and two scores in his return
stories.summary: Daniels came back from a dislocated left elbow and ran nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns, from 38 and 26 yards. He also went 17 of 25 for 199 yards through the air, a 302-yard total day.

stories.text: 302: yards for Daniels passing and running vs. the Giants
stories.summary: Daniels threw for 199 yards and ran for 103 against New York in his first game back from the elbow injury. Terry McLaurin added 4 catches for 62 yards, and Croskey-Merritt ran 11 times for 82 yards and a score.

stories.text: Tonight at San Francisco, then a Week 7 bye
stories.summary: Washington plays the 49ers tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC at Levi's Stadium. The Commanders have a bye in Week 7, then play the Eagles on a Sunday night.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams is back and the Bears are 4-2

stories.text: Williams returns and Bears beat Atlanta 31-23
stories.summary: Caleb Williams came back from a three-game hamstring absence and threw for 305 yards on 30-of-36 passing with one touchdown and no turnovers. He went 10 of 10 for 122 yards on the first two drives, both of which ended in touchdowns. Chicago led 31-7 before Atlanta rallied, and the Bears moved to 4-2.

stories.text: Jackson leaves early as pass rushers stay out
stories.summary: Right guard Jonah Jackson went down in the third quarter and did not return, and he was listed as doubtful right away. Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo did not play, which left the defense without its top pass rushers. Sweat is suspended, and Odeyingbo has a quad injury.

stories.text: Gordon makes his season debut with three sacks
stories.summary: Kyler Gordon had not played this season because of a calf injury. He came back and posted 3 sacks, 4 pressures, 3 tackles for loss and 2 forced fumbles. His strip-sack of Michael Penix Jr. on the last Atlanta drive sealed the win.

stories.text: 12: Bears penalties that cost 133 yards
stories.summary: Chicago was flagged 12 times for 133 yards in Atlanta, eight of them in the first half, and offensive holding wrecked several drives. The Bears still held Bijan Robinson to 61 yards and Atlanta to 3 of 12 on third down. Cleaning up the flags is the obvious fix on a short week.

stories.text: Bears host the Patriots on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago plays New England at Soldier Field on Thursday, Oct. 22, at 8:15 p.m. ET, a short week. It airs on local over-the-air TV rather than Prime Video, so check listings for the channel. The Patriots are 4-2, and the Bears need a clean game with Williams and Gordon back.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions rest after a 45-21 rout in Arizona

stories.text: Lions hit the bye after a 45-21 win in Arizona
stories.summary: Detroit trailed 7-0, then scored on its last seven possessions with the starters to beat the Cardinals and reach 3-2. The win came after Dan Campbell challenged both units following a 32-26 loss to Carolina. The Lions are off this week.

stories.text: Branch and Mays practiced before the bye
stories.summary: Safety Brian Branch and lineman Cade Mays returned to practice the week before the Arizona game but did not play. The Lions have no practices during the bye, so both will condition at the facility with trainers. Detroit's target is a return against Green Bay, with the Vikings game the fallback.

stories.text: Gibbs passes Sanders and tops 200 yards
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs scored twice and finished with 207 scrimmage yards against Arizona. He passed Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns before age 25, with 58. Jared Goff added 279 yards and three scores through the air.

stories.text: 5: sacks from six different Lions in Arizona
stories.summary: Detroit's defense sacked the Cardinals five times, with six players sharing the credit. Keith Abney II had an interception, and Roger McCreary broke up six passes. The offense gained 412 yards and went 4 for 4 on fourth down.

stories.text: Lions host the Packers after the bye
stories.summary: Detroit returns Sunday, Oct. 25, at Ford Field against Green Bay, listed at 4:25 p.m. ET. A second listing shows 3:25 p.m., so confirm the time before kickoff. The Vikings visit the following week.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers handle Dallas for a third straight win

stories.text: Packers beat Dallas 23-13 to reach 4-2
stories.summary: Green Bay built a 17-0 halftime lead on Sunday night at Lambeau Field and held off Dallas for a third straight win. Jordan Love opened the scoring with a 9-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden on a 14-play, 90-yard drive. The Cowboys scored a touchdown in the third quarter but never got closer than two scores.

stories.text: Reed is done for the year, Parsons still out
stories.summary: Receiver Jayden Reed is out for the season with a neck injury, which pushed Christian Watson and Golden into bigger roles. Micah Parsons is still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered last December and sat out Sunday. Newsweek, citing ESPN, said a return in Week 7 at Detroit is his next realistic window.

stories.text: Watson has six touchdown catches through five games
stories.summary: Christian Watson caught six passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns of 42 and 53 yards in the 31-7 win over Chicago. He has 474 receiving yards and six touchdown catches through five games. Golden added 123 yards, and Love called the pair dominant factors.

stories.text: 367: Love's yards on 25-of-31 against Chicago
stories.summary: Jordan Love threw for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in the 31-7 win on Oct. 11. He joined Aaron Rodgers as the only Packers passers with 350 yards, multiple scores, no picks and at least 80 percent completions. The run game still lags, at 70 yards on 26 carries.

stories.text: Packers visit Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at Ford Field, listed at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox, though one schedule shows 3:25 p.m. ET. Watch whether Parsons practices this week. Thursday night, Oct. 29, the Packers host Carolina at Lambeau Field.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings take the bye in first place

stories.text: Vikings are 5-0 heading into the bye
stories.summary: Minnesota beat New Orleans 23-13 on Oct. 11 and sits alone atop the NFC North at 5-0. Kyler Murray ended an eight-quarter touchdown drought with a 15-yard score to Justin Jefferson in the third quarter. The team is off this week.

stories.text: Offensive line takes hits before the bye
stories.summary: Guard Donovan Jackson (knee) is likely out for the regular season, and tight end Josh Oliver (biceps) is out. Tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) and receiver Jordan Addison (hamstring) sat out in New Orleans. T.J. Hockenson left after two plays with a concussion, and the bye gives all of them time.

stories.text: Murray settles in as the offense finds a rhythm
stories.summary: Kyler Murray went 24 of 30 for 229 yards and a touchdown against the Saints. Over the last six quarters he is 40 of 48 for 364 yards with no turnovers, plus 51 rushing yards. He won the starting job over J.J. McCarthy in August and missed time with a concussion in the opener.

stories.text: 39:37: Minnesota's time of possession in New Orleans
stories.summary: The Vikings held the ball for 39:37 to the Saints' 20:23 and outgained them 364 yards to 142. Aaron Jones ran 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. Byron Murphy had two interceptions in the 23-13 win.

stories.text: Bye this week, then the Colts at home
stories.summary: Minnesota is off in Week 6. It returns Sunday, Oct. 25, against Indianapolis at U.S. Bank Stadium, noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on CBS. Check the Darrisaw and Addison status when practice resumes. Detroit comes next on Nov. 1.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons dig another early hole, lose 31-23

stories.text: Falcons fall behind 31-7 and lose a second straight at home
stories.summary: Chicago scored on its first two drives and led 21-7 at the half. Atlanta cut it to 31-23 in the fourth quarter but turned the ball over on downs and then lost a Michael Penix Jr. fumble with about three minutes left. The Falcons are 2-4 and have dropped two straight in Atlanta.

stories.text: Linebackers Deablo and Daniels leave the game hurt
stories.summary: Divine Deablo hurt his arm in the first half and was ruled out. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was carted off on a stretcher in the third quarter. The team said he was alert and moving all his extremities, and he went to Grady Memorial Hospital for evaluation. Billy Bowman Jr. hurt a hamstring late and was doubtful to return, while cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. could come off injured reserve as soon as next week.

stories.text: Penix takes five sacks and loses a late fumble
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. was sacked a season-high five times, and his fumble with about three minutes left ended the comeback. Bijan Robinson finished with a season-low 61 rushing yards on nine carries. The defense gave him little help early, but the protection problems were the story.

stories.text: 11: Cam Thomas sets a career high in QB hits
stories.summary: Cam Thomas landed his 11th quarterback hit of the season against Chicago, a career high and the most on the team. He also has 18 pressures and two sacks. Tackles Gervon Dexter and Brandon Dorlus each added a sack for Chicago, so the Falcons' own rush has work to do too.

stories.text: 49ers (5-0) visit Atlanta Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: San Francisco arrives unbeaten for the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Atlanta had only 97 total yards and four first downs in the first half Sunday and lost the time of possession battle 22:13 to 7:47. Watch whether the Falcons can start fast and keep their defense off the field.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers win in Philly, 25-14

stories.text: Panthers beat banged-up Eagles 25-14 on the road
stories.summary: Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tommy Tremble, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards. Carolina outgained Philadelphia 399-222 and improved to 3-2. The Eagles have lost four straight and played without Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley.

stories.text: Phillips tweaks hamstring, Incoom hurts calf
stories.summary: Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring, aggravated) and Thomas Incoom (calf) were hurt in Philadelphia. Neither status for next week was reported. Carolina also played with backup corners after Jaycee Horn went to injured reserve.

stories.text: Tremble catches both Young touchdowns
stories.summary: Tommy Tremble caught four passes for 46 yards and scored from 12 and 19 yards, the second with 6:33 left to seal the game. Jalen Coker led all receivers with six catches for 97 yards, and Tetairoa McMillan had six for 86. Young went 20 of 39 with no interceptions.

stories.text: 11: Fitzgerald's straight field goals to open the year
stories.summary: Kicker Ryan Fitzgerald hit from 47 and 52 yards in Philadelphia, and the 52-yarder was his 11th straight make to start the season. He did miss an extra point. Carolina was also flagged 13 times for 149 yards, and the coach blamed players trying too hard.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Charlotte Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is 1-5 and comes to Bank of America Stadium for the first division game of its season. Carolina leads the NFC South. Watch the penalty count, which cannot run to 13 again.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints rally from 10 down to beat Giants

stories.text: Saints erase a 10-point hole and beat Giants 34-27
stories.summary: New Orleans trailed 10-0, then scored on five straight drives and led 34-10 before the Giants made a late run. The Saints are 2-4 and snapped a losing streak. The defense had five sacks and four takeaways.

stories.text: Kamara and Olave questionable, then both score
stories.summary: Alvin Kamara (back) and Chris Olave (illness) were listed questionable Friday, and linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and edge Anfernee Jennings (knee) were out. Kamara and Olave both scored touchdowns Sunday. Quarterback Tyler Shough's left hand was a full participant.

stories.text: Shough accounts for four touchdowns
stories.summary: Tyler Shough went 16 of 30 for 144 yards and three touchdowns and added a quarterback sneak for a fourth score. He also ran five times for 32 yards. Bryce Lance caught his first NFL touchdown from him just before halftime.

stories.text: 175: Saints rush for a season high
stories.summary: New Orleans ran for 175 yards against the Giants. Kendre Miller had 20 carries for 74 yards, CJ Donaldson added 39 and Kamara 34. Kamara also became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 career rushing and receiving yards.

stories.text: Saints meet Steelers in Paris Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFLN
stories.summary: The game is at Stade de France in Saint-Denis. New Orleans has to travel overseas on a short turnaround after the win. Watch whether the run game and the pass rush carry over.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs blow 16-3 lead, lose in overtime

stories.text: Bucs squander a 16-3 lead and lose to Steelers in overtime
stories.summary: Tampa Bay led 16-3 entering the fourth quarter, then Pittsburgh scored on five straight possessions and won 26-19 in overtime. The Bucs are 1-5. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels started in place of Baker Mayfield.

stories.text: Mayfield out with a dislocated thumb
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield missed the game with a dislocated thumb, and no return date has been reported. Running back Sean Tucker (quad) was ruled out and rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter played through a knee issue.

stories.text: Daniels throws two picks in a long day
stories.summary: Jalon Daniels went 22 of 43 for 164 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Jalen Ramsey sacked him on third down early and again on the fourth down that ended the game. Emeka Egbuka had seven catches for 48 yards and a score.

stories.text: 5: Bucs sack Aaron Rodgers five times and still lose
stories.summary: David Walker had two sacks and rookie Rueben Bain Jr. got his first. Chase McLaughlin made four field goals, from 43, 47, 33 and 53 yards. The defense held up for three quarters, but the offense could not close.

stories.text: Bucs at Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: It is Tampa Bay's first division game, against the NFC South leader and Bryce Young. Mayfield's thumb will decide who plays quarterback. The Bucs host Atlanta on November 1.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Ryland's sixth field goal beats the Rams

stories.text: Cardinals steal one at SoFi on a buzzer beater
stories.summary: Arizona beat the Rams 18-16 as a double-digit underdog and moved to 2-4. Chad Ryland hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired, three plays after Los Angeles took the lead with under a minute left. It was Mike LaFleur's first win over his former boss, Sean McVay.

stories.text: Nolen hurts an ankle, Love sits again
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Walter Nolen III left for part of the fourth quarter with an ankle injury, and LaFleur had no diagnosis afterward. Running back Jeremiyah Love missed the game, and Bam Knight dealt with cramps in the humidity. Watch the Wednesday practice report for both linemen and backs.

stories.text: Ryland drills six field goals, including the winner
stories.summary: Kicker Chad Ryland made six field goals at SoFi, the last from 43 yards at the buzzer. Jalen Brooks' 21-yard catch and a roughing penalty on the Rams moved Arizona into range. Ryland's six kicks accounted for all of the Cardinals' 18 points.

stories.text: 80: Bam Knight's rushing yards in Love's place
stories.summary: With Jeremiyah Love out, Knight ran 15 times for 80 yards. The defense also had its best day of the year, holding the Rams to 286 yards and keeping an opponent under 30 points for the first time since Week 1.

stories.text: Broncos visit Glendale on Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Denver on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Broncos lead with defense, so watch whether the Cardinals protect the passer and keep the run game alive if Love stays out.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams sit last in the West after home loss

stories.text: Rams fall to 2-4 as McVay owns the slide
stories.summary: Los Angeles lost 18-16 to Arizona and now sits last in the NFC West. The Rams are the fifth outright preseason Super Bowl favorite in 50 years to have a losing record through six games. McVay said it is his job to get the team playing with more consistent energy.

stories.text: Kicker, receiver and cornerback all in question
stories.summary: Kicker Blake Grupe hurt his knee on a tackle just after his first kick as a Ram, and punter Ethan Evans finished the game kicking. Davante Adams went down with a non-contact left knee injury, with no diagnosis yet. Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett did not play Sunday.

stories.text: Stafford efficient but hit at the wrong time
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford went 25 of 32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. A blindside hit from Josh Sweat caused a fumble, and the offense failed on both fourth-down tries.

stories.text: 286: total yards in the loss to Arizona
stories.summary: The Rams scored 16 points on 286 yards against a defense that came in as one of the league's worst. Pre-snap penalties, turnovers and two failed fourth downs stalled drives.

stories.text: Rams head to Las Vegas on Sunday
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at the Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The kicker spot needs sorting out first. The Rams have not signed anyone since Grupe's injury as of Sunday's reports.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Unbeaten 49ers host Washington on Monday night

stories.text: 49ers chase 6-0 on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: San Francisco is 5-0 and can extend its NFC West lead tonight against Washington. The Seahawks and Rams both lost this week, and each has now dropped two straight. Only the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings remain unbeaten.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans and Samuel sat Friday
stories.summary: Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) did not practice on Friday. James Thompson Jr. returned as a limited participant, and Kyle Juszczyk practiced fully with a knee issue. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw serves a one-game suspension.

stories.text: McCaffrey's workload is being managed
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey has 61 carries for 286 yards and five touchdowns, plus 19 catches for 137 yards. Kyle Shanahan wants to rotate him so he stays fresh late in games, and rookie Kaelon Black has 37 carries for 136 yards.

stories.text: 5: sacks of Sam Darnold in the win over Seattle
stories.summary: San Francisco beat Seattle 32-29 behind five sacks and four forced turnovers. The win snapped the Seahawks' nine-game home winning streak.

stories.text: Commanders tonight, then Atlanta
stories.summary: The 49ers host Washington tonight, Monday, Oct. 19, at 8:15 p.m. ET at Levi's Stadium on Monday Night Football. Next up is a trip to Atlanta on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks stay with Darnold after OT loss

stories.text: Macdonald keeps Darnold as the starter
stories.summary: Coach Mike Macdonald said there is no change at quarterback after Denver beat Seattle 17-14 in overtime on Thursday. Darnold has seven interceptions since returning from injury. Seattle is 3-3, the same loss total it had all of last season.

stories.text: Charbonnet has a real shot to return
stories.summary: Zach Charbonnet, recovering from a torn ACL, has a legitimate chance to make his season debut against Kansas City, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. He must be activated by Oct. 22 or revert to injured reserve. Rookie Jadarian Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba finishes with 12 catches for 134
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards against Denver, after only two catches for 11 yards in the first half. He was the one steady piece of an offense that struggled to score.

stories.text: 51: career-high pass attempts for Darnold
stories.summary: Darnold threw a career-high 51 passes for 278 yards and a 52.6 rating. Seattle has 12 turnovers through six games, seven of them Darnold interceptions.

stories.text: Chiefs come to Seattle on Sunday night
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Kansas City on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Chiefs were 5-0 as of Sunday, so the offense has to protect the ball.
